cards.stem: Which tally is shown for affirmative votes on the resolution in the document?
cards.quote: The document seen here shows the vote on the Lee Resolution — the affirmative votes of 12 colonies are listed at the right.
cards.hint: Look at the list shown at the right side of the document.

cards.stem: Who introduced the resolution proposing that the colonies become independent?
cards.quote: On June 7, 1776, Richard Henry Lee introduced a resolution
cards.hint: Think about who acted under instruction from Virginia.

cards.stem: Which part was included in the three parts of the resolution?
cards.quote: a declaration of independence, a call to form foreign alliances, and "a plan for confederation."
cards.hint: Recall the first element listed among the three parts.

cards.stem: What did the Congress create in response to the resolution on June 11, 1776?
cards.quote: On June 11, 1776, the Congress appointed three concurrent committees in response to the Lee Resolution
cards.hint: Consider how the Congress divided the work of the resolution.

every card's correct answer options[0] occurs in its quote after normalisation, with any numbers matching as whole signed numbers (answer-in-quote)
every card has distinct options after normalisation, with no two options spelling the same number (options-distinct)
no stem contains its own correct answer (stem-no-answer-leak)
exactly one option per card matches the quote (one-correct)
every number in stems, options and hints appears on the cited page or in the same quote as that whole signed number (N-01) (numbers-checkable)
no distractor occurs in its card quote (distractors-not-in-quote)
